extracted.intended_audience: Registered apprenticeship program sponsors, participating employers, Registration Agencies (including State Apprenticeship Agencies), and Department of Labor officials/oversight staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedures for recordkeeping, program reviews, compliance action plans, enforcement options (including suspension and deregistration), appeals/hearings, reinstatement, and exemptions under proposed revisions to 29 CFR part 29.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping to demonstrate compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors must maintain records demonstrating program compliance with registered apprenticeship requirements; this could include documents maintained for purposes of compliance with registered apprenticeship requirements in Federal grants such as WIOA, the IRA, the Davis-Bacon and related Acts, and any Federal purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records should be sufficient to show compliance with registered apprenticeship requirements and related Federal grant conditions; failure to preserve complete and accurate records constitutes noncompliance and could lead to deregistration proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention period (5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Records required by this part and any other information relevant to compliance must be maintained by a program sponsor (or any participating employer, if applicable) for 5 years from the date of the making of the record or the personnel action involved, whichever occurs later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 5-year timeframe aligns with 29 CFR 30.12 and proposed §29.19 program review frequency; consistency across parts 29 and 30 is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency access to records
rubrics_metrics.description: Program sponsors (and participating employers) must allow the Registration Agency access to records upon request for purposes of conducting program reviews and investigating complaints; this may include inspecting and copying books, accounts, records (including electronic records), and any other material the Registration Agency deems relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors must provide information about all formats (including specific electronic formats) in which records are available; information obtained will be used only in connection with administration of the part or other applicable laws. Language mirrors part 30 provisions to ensure uniformity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records must be available regardless of medium
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms, records, and any other documents used and maintained by the program sponsor (and any participating employer) may exist in paper or electronic form or a combination thereof, but regardless of the medium these records must be available and accessible as required for oversight and compliance purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accessibility obligations apply equally to paper and electronic records; sponsors should ensure timely access and the ability to produce records in the requested format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program review frequency (at least every 5 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a program's registration is made permanent, the applicable Registration Agency must conduct a program review at least every 5 years, though more frequent reviews are permitted based on capacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with existing requirements for compliance reviews and the 5-year recordkeeping requirement; new programs undergo an initial provisional review (~1 year) then move to 5-year cycle if operating per standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include participating employers in program reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Registration Agency will include a review of any participating employers in a sponsor's program during program reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes oversight and accountability for participating employers' compliance where appropriate and connects them to the sponsor-focused review mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program reviews triggered by credible information
rubrics_metrics.description: A Registration Agency must conduct a review of a program if it receives credible information that a program, participating employer, or other registered apprenticeship stakeholder is not operating in compliance with the program's accepted standards or other requirements; credible information can include complaints, referrals, or news stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrator may also request reviews; referrals and news stories may prompt an initial review or further investigation if additional facts are needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of all pertinent information and program performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration Agencies may consider all information and data pertinent to the purpose of the review in reaching a determination and must consider the program's performance under §29.25(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of program performance ensures technical assistance can be provided and program improvement needs are identified during the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with interviews and document requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsors and participating employers must cooperate with requests for interviews and documentation from the Registration Agency and may never impede the Agency's ability to interview prospective, current, or former apprentices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration Agencies may draw adverse inferences if a sponsor or participating employer declines to answer, gives evasive answers, or fails to produce required records; cooperation is essential for efficient and effective program reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Notice of Program Review Findings
rubrics_metrics.description: At the conclusion of a program review, the Registration Agency must provide a Notice of Program Review Findings containing a summary of any noncompliance identified, a concise explanation as to how the noncompliance may be cured, an explanation that the sponsor must develop a compliance action plan, and a statement that enforcement action may be taken if compliance is not achieved within an established timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice is designed to make the sponsor aware of concerns and the steps needed to address noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor timeframe to rebut or submit compliance action plan (45 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a Notice of Program Review Findings details one or more areas of noncompliance, the sponsor is afforded 45 calendar days from the date of notification to either rebut the findings or submit a compliance action plan; this period may be extended once by the Registration Agency for up to 45 additional days for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 45-day period is longer than the 30 days in 29 CFR 30.15 to avoid being shorter than related EEO timelines; good cause examples include staffing changes affecting responsible personnel. The Registration Agency has discretion to determine whether a rebuttal is successful.

rubrics_metrics.name: If rebuttal rejected, additional 45 days to submit plan
rubrics_metrics.description: If a sponsor submits a rebuttal that the Registration Agency in its discretion does not find to rebut the Findings, the sponsor is afforded 45 calendar days from receipt of the final notice to submit a compliance action plan for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a separate opportunity to submit a corrective plan after a rebuttal is resolved unfavorably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum content required in a compliance action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A compliance action plan must (1) make a specific written commitment to correct/remediate identified deficiencies/noncompliance, (2) specify actions to remedy each deficiency, (3) specify a timeline within which each deficiency will be remedied and any program changes implemented, and (4) provide the name of the individual(s) responsible for correcting each deficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should be concrete and assign clear responsibility and timelines; lack of specificity may lead to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration Agency options after reviewing compliance action plan
rubrics_metrics.description: After reviewing a compliance action plan, a Registration Agency may (1) approve the plan, determine the sponsor is in compliance, and terminate the review; (2) approve the plan but continue the review until the plan is appropriately implemented; or (3) reject the plan and proceed with deregistration per §29.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may work with sponsors to revise rejected plans instead of immediately deregistering; continued monitoring may be used when implementation must be verified (e.g., registering a first apprentice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement options and graduated remedies prior to deregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon determining a violation, a Registration Agency could: (1) offer technical assistance to promote compliance; (2) require submission of a compliance action plan; (3) suspend the sponsor's right to register new apprentices for a specified time period; and/or (4) deregister the program for cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options may be used singly or concurrently; technical assistance is appropriate for misunderstandings, suspension is appropriate when safety concerns exist, and deregistration is a last resort when correction fails or violations are egregious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deregistration standard and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Any program not operated in accordance with parts 29 or 30 may be deregistered if the sponsor fails to correct violations or fails to obtain approval of and implement an approvable compliance action plan within required timeframes; determinations about approvability and implementation are at the sole discretion of the Registration Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed §29.20 removes ambiguous bases for deregistration (e.g., 'persistent and significant failure') and streamlines the standard to compliance with parts 29 and 30; appeal timing is adjusted so appeals arise after a Notice of Deregistration (i.e., ripe decisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirements for deregistration process
rubrics_metrics.description: The deregistration process begins with notifying the sponsor or participating employer of specific violations identified via program review, complaint investigation, or 'any other basis'; the notice may identify remedial actions or that the program is deregistered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices are similar to Notices of Program Review Findings but may reference a broader set of options (including immediate deregistration); participating employers can be offered technical assistance though only the sponsor may suspend a participating employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrator review required for SAA-issued deregistrations
rubrics_metrics.description: When a State Apprenticeship Agency (SAA) issues a Notice of Deregistration, the Administrator will review the SAA's decision through a three-step process: (1) Informal Resolution by the Administrator; (2) Appeal to the Office of Administrative Law Judges (OALJ); and (3) Appeal to the Administrative Review Board (ARB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This required Administrator review is intended to resolve novel issues in the first instance, conserve Department resources, and in some cases (e.g., failure to respond or failure to register at least one apprentice) the Administrator's review outcome will be the Department's final agency determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines and procedures for requests for review and hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Former sponsors must submit requests for Administrator review electronically and in writing within 30 calendar days of the Notice of Deregistration. For SAA cases, the SAA must provide the Administrator a record within 15 calendar days. Except where deregistration is based on failure to respond or to register at least one apprentice, a former sponsor may request a hearing before the OALJ within 15 calendar days of the Administrator's final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests need not follow a prescribed format but must present relevant facts and documentation; hearing requests must also be furnished to the Associate Solicitor for Employment and Training Legal Services; the Administrator compiles the administrative file for the OALJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing procedures and standard of review
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for hearings are not complaints requiring an answer; limited pre-hearing motions and discovery may be permitted at the ALJ's discretion; the Administrative Law Judge will apply an 'arbitrary and capricious' standard of review to uphold the Administrator's decision unless shown otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intent is efficient adjudication often on the administrative record; the ALJ may allow limited additional procedures when necessary but generally will rely on the compiled administrative file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement of deregistered program registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A deregistered apprenticeship program may have its registration reinstated if the prospective sponsor submits adequate evidence that the program is operating in compliance with parts 29 and 30; a parallel reinstatement process exists for former sponsors with active but unregistered programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include post-deregistration evidence that at least one apprentice has been registered and an adequate explanation for prior failure; determinations of what constitutes adequate evidence lie exclusively with the Registration Agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption requests and limits (subpart A only)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator may entertain written requests for exemptions from any or all provisions of subpart A of 29 CFR part 29; requests must state reasons and exemptions are granted only for good cause (e.g., expanding or supporting apprentice safety/welfare) and will not reduce statutory protections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAAs are excluded from exemption consideration; exemptions will not apply to subpart B (except considerations for CTE sponsors) or subpart C (data and SAA governance) given the rulemaking priorities; the Department requests comment on criteria for 'good cause'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping noncompliance as basis for enforcement/deregistration
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to preserve complete and accurate records (as required by the recordkeeping paragraph) constitutes noncompliance with the part and could lead to OA initiating deregistration proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors should ensure completeness and accuracy of records to avoid enforcement; recordkeeping is explicitly tied to compliance posture and potential sanctions.
